## Programs at the Université de Moncton

The lab is based at the École de foresterie on the Edmundston campus, close to the Acadian forest and with strong ties to industry partners.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Language.** The Université de Moncton is a French-language university. Students need working French for courses, exams, presentations and reports. Research work and publications can be in English if you prefer.
:::

:::: {.card-grid}

::: {.tile}
[Undergraduate]{.eyebrow}

### Bachelor of Management in Forest Resources

A solid foundation in forest ecology, geomatics and sustainable management.

[Program details](https://www.umoncton.ca/umce-foresterie/){.more}
:::

::: {.tile}
[Master's]{.eyebrow}

### Master in Forest Sciences (M.Sc.F.)

Thesis-based projects on climate change impacts and adaptive silviculture, with field sites in the Acadian forest and close links to industry.

[Program details](https://www.umoncton.ca/umce-foresterie/sites/umce-foresterie.prod.umoncton.ca/files/wf/brocmscf.pdf){.more}
:::

::: {.tile}
[Doctoral]{.eyebrow}

### PhD in Life Sciences

Thesis-based doctoral research in forestry: climate change impacts, forest management and adaptive silviculture, with opportunities to mentor and collaborate with students on applied projects.

[Program details](https://www.umoncton.ca/node/341?programme=241){.more}
:::

::::

## Studying at another university

Research often spans several institutions. Dr. Albert co-supervises MSc and PhD students registered at partner universities, and can help put together a project and a supervisory committee. We currently have collaborators at:

- **Université Laval**, Faculté de foresterie, de géographie et de géomatique
- **University of New Brunswick**, Forestry and Environmental Management

## How to apply

Send an email to [cedric.albert@umoncton.ca](mailto:cedric.albert@umoncton.ca) with:

1. A short statement of interest: which project or topic, and why
2. Your CV
3. Unofficial transcripts
